summary: the file is not a table the reader can follow (a quote never closed, text after a closing quote, a cell too long, semicolons for commas), holds no event_type column or holds a header and no rows, so nothing in it was checked
fix: Save the records as CSV with commas or TSV with tabs, a header row and one row for each critical tracking event (docs/inputs.md); fix the line named.

summary: a column that the rows of a kind of event need is not in the header at all, so the element cannot be given in any of those rows; it is reported once, at the header, and not for each row
fix: Add the column named to the spreadsheet and fill it for the rows that need it; docs/inputs.md lists every column.

summary: a column the tool does not read, often a misspelt name; nothing under it was checked
fix: Correct the name to a column of docs/inputs.md, or leave the column in if it is for your own use.

summary: two columns of the header have the same name once case and separators are ignored; only the first is read
fix: Keep one column of each name.

summary: a row with more or fewer cells than the header, which usually means a comma that is not in quotes; the row was left out of every other check
fix: Put a cell that holds a comma, a tab or a line end in double quotes, and write a quote inside it as two quotes.

summary: the file holds a private key, a seed or a mnemonic, under a column named for one or as a cell shaped like one; the tool never reads it and never shows it
fix: Remove the value from the file and from wherever the file was copied, treat it as exposed and move what it controls to a new key. A traceability record names food, lots, places and documents, never the key of an account.

summary: an event_type that is empty or is none of the seven critical tracking events of 1.1310: harvesting, cooling, initial packing, first land-based receiving, shipping, receiving and making a new product ("transformation" in the file); the row was left out of the element checks
fix: Write one of "harvesting", "cooling", "initial_packing", "first_land_based_receiving", "shipping", "receiving" or "transformation" in the event_type column.

summary: a key data element that the section of the rule lists for the kind of event is empty or a placeholder such as n/a: the lot code, the product description, the quantity and unit, a location description of the right party, a date, the reference document type or number, and for making a new product the inputs; the message names the section
fix: Fill the element named in the cell named, from the business record the row comes from; docs/inputs.md says which column holds each element.

summary: the field, growing area or container of a harvest or an initial packing is empty; the rule asks for it for produce and for aquacultured food, and the file does not say which food the row is about
fix: Name the field, growing area or container as the grower does; leave it empty only for a food that is neither produce nor aquacultured.

summary: a row for harvesting or cooling holds a traceability lot code, though the rule assigns one at initial packing, first land-based receiving or making a new product, and sets no lot code for other activities
fix: Leave the lot code out of the harvesting and cooling rows; the packer assigns it when it initially packs the food.

summary: a shipping row names the shipping location as the lot code source, but no row of the file assigns that lot code (initial packing, first land-based receiving, making a new product, or receiving); the rule says not to establish a new lot code when shipping
fix: Ship the food under the lot code it already has, and add the row of the event that assigned it; if the lot code came from elsewhere, name that place as the lot code source.

summary: a cell of a date column that is not a date, or names a day that does not exist, or is written as a date of the United States; the date of the event is a key data element
fix: Write the date as YYYY-MM-DD: four digits for the year, two for the month and two for the day.

summary: a quantity with no unit of measure, or a unit of measure with no quantity; the rule asks for the quantity and the unit together
fix: Give the unit of measure with the quantity, such as cases, pounds or kg, and the quantity with the unit.

summary: a quantity that is not a plain positive number: zero, negative, with a thousands separator, with an exponent or text
fix: Write the quantity as a plain number above zero, such as 25 or 12.5, with no unit in the cell.
own: asking for a positive plain number is a best practice of this tool, not a rule of 21 CFR Part 1 Subpart S; the rule asks for a quantity and says nothing about how it is written, but a quantity of zero or one that is text cannot be added up or compared

summary: a date later than the moment given with --now (a day alone is allowed one day more, for the time zones of the world); without --now the check does not run
fix: Correct the date or the clock of the system that wrote it; an event cannot be recorded before it took place.
own: refusing a date from the future is a best practice of this tool, not a rule of 21 CFR Part 1 Subpart S; the rule sets none, and the tool reads no clock, so the moment is the one given with --now

summary: the dates of one row come in the wrong order: harvest_date, cooling_date, receipt_date and event_date should not go back
fix: Check each date against the business record; food cannot be received before it is harvested or packed before it is received.
own: comparing the dates of a row this way is a best practice of this tool, not a rule of 21 CFR Part 1 Subpart S; the rule asks for each date and does not say how they relate, but food moves forward through its events

summary: a receiving row whose lot code is not shipped by any shipping row of the file; a note, because a file of one firm holds the receipts of food shipped by others
fix: If the file is meant to hold both sides of the move, add the shipping row or correct the lot code; if it holds one firm, no change is needed.
own: matching a receipt with a shipment is a best practice of this tool, not a rule of 21 CFR Part 1 Subpart S; the rule asks each firm to keep its own records and does not ask for the two sides in one file, so this is a note

summary: a shipping row whose lot code is not received by any receiving row of the file; a note, because the recipient keeps its own records
fix: If the file is meant to hold both sides of the move, add the receiving row or correct the lot code; if it holds one firm, no change is needed.
own: matching a shipment with a receipt is a best practice of this tool, not a rule of 21 CFR Part 1 Subpart S; the rule asks each firm to keep its own records and does not ask for the two sides in one file, so this is a note

summary: the receiving rows of a lot code add up to more than the shipping rows of the same lot code in the same unit of measure
fix: Check the quantity and the unit of the receiving row named, and whether a shipping row of that lot is missing from the file.
own: adding up the quantities of a lot is a best practice of this tool, not a rule of 21 CFR Part 1 Subpart S; the rule says nothing about how much may be received, but a lot cannot arrive in a larger amount than was sent, and a file that holds only some of the shipments can show this by mistake

summary: a row for making a new product names an input lot code that no row of the file holds
fix: Check the input lot code against the record of the receipt, or add the row that holds it; the input lot should be received, packed or made earlier in the file.
own: following an input lot back to a row is a best practice of this tool, not a rule of 21 CFR Part 1 Subpart S; the rule asks for the input lot codes and does not ask that the file holds the row that explains each one, and a file that holds only some of the records can show this by mistake

summary: a row whose cells are all the same as an earlier row, which counts one event twice
fix: Delete the repeated row, or correct the cell that should differ.
own: looking for repeated rows is a best practice of this tool, not a rule of 21 CFR Part 1 Subpart S; the rule does not mention them, but a repeated row doubles the quantity of a lot
